column1: # Sweep generations for the #84 UNKNOWN-rate measurement. One row per sweep.
# A generation is one run of sweep.sh: one engine build, one set of images,
# one artifacts directory. The rulebook's "one sweep, one engine build" rule
# lives here rather than in prose, because A and B need not be measured in
# the same generation — #239 re-sweeps A while leaving B's 2026-08-16
# measurement in place, and the threshold is set from B alone.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   id  date  artifacts_dir  groups  status
# date: the sweep's date, or "-" when it has not run.
# artifacts_dir: relative to spike/unknown-rate/.
# groups: comma-separated, no spaces. The groups this generation measures.
# status: exactly two values are accepted here.
#   complete   the manifest exists and matches this generation's expected
#              trial set exactly — every row with since <= id in a covered
#              group, in corpus order.
#   unstarted  no manifest. docs must carry the not-yet-measured placeholder.
# There is deliberately no third value for the state between them. A manifest
# that covers some of its expected rows is a half-measured sweep, and a rate
# computed from one is indistinguishable, once published, from a rate
# computed from all of them — so that state is detected (count.py check
# compares the manifest against the expected set and refuses) rather than
# recorded. Writing "partial" here is itself an error: the point is that a
# half-finished sweep has nowhere to be written down and therefore nowhere
# to be published from.
# A generation is never edited after it goes complete. Re-measuring means a
# new row here and a new artifacts directory; the old numbers stay published
# beside the new ones with both dates, because the movement is the finding.
